S14).

Cluster 1 CD103 −/low T RM cells also expressed higher levels of NKG7, a cytotoxic molecule that can promote lethal inflammation after infection ( 22 ), and granzyme K, an inflammatory granzyme that promotes fibroblast activation ( Fig. 4B and figs. S6F and S14F) ( 23 ) .

Compared with age-matched or unmatched healthy controls, aged COVID-19 convalescents had increased presence of cluster 2 CD4 + T cells, which expressed genes associated with myeloid cell inflammation including Lyz, S100 A8, and S100 A9 (fig. S11, K to M) ( 21 ).
